claims.statement: Chang’an was the Western Han capital. Palaces, residential districts and markets occupied a city organised along a north–south axis. It provides an urban setting for the dynasty’s rulers, writers and trade.

Chang’an under the Western Han: 206 BCE to 9 CE. Western Han study window, not foundation dates or an assertion that it was the capital from the first year. Precise geographic reference not yet checked.
Weiyang Palace site reference within Han Chang’an. This point locates the existing study window; it does not date every structure, define the city’s boundaries or establish any person’s presence.
